s12f-transformed-masks.summaryMarkdown:
**Verdict: passed at revision 233 (snapshot 4d9d947a), first review of `s12f-transformed-masks`.** The cause is as the coordinator found it, I confirmed it independently, and the fix is the right cut. No finding.

**Cause, independently.** In my second s12e review's bisection the difference needed scroll layers together with retained layout and views (mechanism bits 1011 and 1111), never without scroll layers. At this head the same ten combinations (`p103`, a bordered transformed row, scale 2) all show 0 differing steps. The mask arithmetic: a transformed element's clip mask is the bounding box of its transformation of `clip intersected with content mask`; the layered content mask is the painted region (viewport plus overscan), so the box of the turned strip was looser than the reference's box of the strip cut by the viewport. `transformed_clip` cuts the logical clip by the painting's viewport first, which is the reference's mask: the viewport is `window.content_mask()` when the container begins (the container's own clip with everything above it), and what is inside the container is cut by `with_content_mask` as before, so nested containers, nested and ancestor transformed elements and intermediate clips reproduce `clip, viewport and everything above`. The hook sits in `with_content_mask_telling`, which `with_untold_content_mask` and the border path share; culling (`content_mask_stack`) and every untransformed mask are untouched, and the reference window is not affected (`painting` is `None`).

**What I ran** (probes in the scratchpad, this head against its base `538edae`; layered window with every mechanism against the reference with snapping forced, 476 steps of single pixels, wheel runs and mixed steps unless noted).
- Matrix of transformed content, 95 reports at scales 1, 1.25, 1.3333, 2 and 2.625 (the first three kinds also at 1.25): bordered rounded shadowed rows turned, moved and scaled (each kind alone and mixed); a rotated, moved or scaled *ancestor* holding bordered children; a transformed card clipping underlined text and a path; a transformed bordered child inside an `overflow_hidden` card; in a `div`, nested scrolling containers, a `uniform_list` and a `list`: 0 of 95 differ at the head, 73 of 95 differ at the base (up to 170 levels), the same kinds as the report and more (text, underline and path rows, ancestor-transformed rows, the nested child). A transformed container itself (never layered): equal at both. Cards moved 70 px out of their rows, so that rows in the overscan show in view, with and without a border: equal at the head (the border ones differed at the base). Culling holds: the viewport cut leaves what is outside the viewport out.
- Transformed, then not, then promoted again: 246 steps with the transform toggled every 30 and 362 steps with it going away: 0 differ at the head (3 to 4 and 2 differed at the base); after it goes the container is composited again, 298 composited steps, the same count at the base.
- Frames across commits: 45 315 frame pairs of transformed content: the reference window is identical at both commits in all, and the layered window differs from the base in 191 (the repair) and from its own reference in 0; 19 080 frame pairs of untransformed bordered, tiny, rounded, clipped and one pixel rows (`div`, nested, `uniform_list`, `list`, scales 1.25 and 2): identical at both in both windows.
- Regression: `p80`, `p81`, `p86`, `p83` (221 comparisons at 8 scales, transformed groups of LYR-15 among them) 0 differing steps; the lane C groups at the head (`lane_c_scroll_layers` 18, `lane_c_layer_scales` 7 with the new group, `lane_c_list_hover` 2) pass; `fast::` unit tests 424 of 424; the sprint's checks (39 lane A scenes, the new unit test, the new pixel group) and Linux log pass. The new unit test fails with the hook removed and with its condition inverted.

**Not blocking.** The shipped tests hold one content (rounded bordered cards turned, moved and scaled). The fix is general and my probes show text, underline, path, ancestor-transformed and nested transformed rows were broken at the base and are right at the head, but a change that kept only the border case would pass the shipped tests; the criterion names those groups. A second content of a transformed card clipping underlined text and a path (my variant 7) would guard the rest.

No tracked file touched; scratch worktrees and probe profiles removed.

findings.descriptionMarkdown:
**Resolved.** The cause was that `gpui_platform`'s `bench-support` did not enable `font-kit`, so macOS benches drew with `NoopTextSystem`. `bench-support` now enables `font-kit`.

The recaptured baseline paints glyphs:
- `still-frame/off`: 7,766 primitives a frame (was 60).
- `scroll-child-view`: 120 a frame (was 31).
- `hover-sweep`: 310 a frame (was 80).

Every text scenario's `expect` now applies `drawn_per_frame`, which is shared by the bench and the attribution group.

The scroll scenarios' floor has since been raised to 60 primitives a frame (86441c0), above their 31 row backgrounds, so each of them now fails on its own if the glyphs are missing.

**Resolved.** `perf fast-mode` now records `Tree: clean|N uncommitted changes` from `git status --porcelain`, and this is tested in `fast_mode_report.rs`.

The baseline was recaptured at `24d413c` with `Tree: clean`, and `docs/fast-mode.md` names `24d413c`. The only later change, `88326e6`, touches `docs/fast-mode.md` alone, so `24d413c` is the measured source. The baseline also keeps `medians.txt`.

**Resolved.** FM-2, the d-switches invariants and `docs/fast-mode.md` ("Cached views and hovers") now declare the cached-view hover dependency as gpux behaviour in every mode.

The one-frame lag is gone: `paint_view` notes a replay whose hovers changed (`note_stale_replay`), and `Window::draw` draws the frame again before it is shown (`redraw_stale_replays` followed by a second `draw_frame`). I checked the side effects of the discarded first frame: snapshot requests are not drained, and the focus diff, arena clear and input handler are idempotent.

The regression test `cached_view_drops_its_hover_in_the_frame_an_overlay_covers_it` exercises the covered case. The oracle now has `CoverCells` (an occluding overlay over the first grid row) and `HoverCell`, and it compares the first frame after each step (`set_draw_on_flush(false)`).

**Resolved.** Medians now come from Criterion's `target/criterion/<id>/new/estimates.json` (`parse_median`, `apply_medians`). They are kept per run in `medians.txt` for `--compare`.

The column reads "Median" only when medians were found, and "Estimate" with a note otherwise. The baseline's `medians.txt` holds a median for every id. This is tested by `medians_come_from_criterion_estimates`.
**Resolved.** `cargo fmt --check` passes (re-run by the reviewer).

**Resolved (86441c0).** `redraw_stale_replays(&mut Window)` now marks each stale view and its ancestors with `Window::mark_view_dirty`, which walks the rendered frame's dispatch tree into `window.dirty_views`. It no longer uses the invalidator, `Effect::Notify` or the platform waker.

`dirty_views` is cleared during the first draw and not reset when the second `draw_frame` starts. So the second draw rebuilds those views, because `prepaint_view` checks `!window.dirty_views.contains`.

The overlay regression test now registers `cx.observe(&cell, ..)` and asserts, after `run_until_parked`, that the observer never ran.

**Resolved (ec42016).** `fast::dependencies::hover_area` checks every hover the view read against the hitboxes in its own prepaint range. One read of a hitbox the view did not insert, such as an ancestor's group, makes the area `HoverArea::Foreign`, and `may_replay_hovers` never replays such a view. `view.rs` computes the area after prepaint and recomputes it after paint when paint read hovers.

This goes further than the repair the review suggested (recording the foreign hitbox's bounds), and is correct. An ancestor that is rebuilt reinserts its group hitbox under a new id, so a replayed foreign read names a dead id. The replayed group-hover mouse listener has the same problem. A cell replayed once would stay unhovered for good, a defect `cached_view_reading_a_group_hover_follows_the_group_its_owner_redraws` now proves.

Hitboxes a nested cached view replays keep their ids inside the parent's range, so they still count as the parent's own. The reviewer's overlay scenario is now `cached_view_reading_a_group_hover_drops_it_when_an_overlay_covers_the_group`, which asserts the unhovered background with zero replays. A positive control keeps own-hover views replayable away from the pointer. The oracle's grid cells read the row's group hover. The spec (FM-5, d-hover-area) is amended to match.

**Resolved (962e47e).** The abandoned-press branch in `div.rs` now calls `cx.notify(current_view)`, like the clicking branch. The inspector's kept refresh carries a "Whole-window:" comment.

`active_and_hover_styles_redraw_their_view` adds press-again and release-elsewhere frames. They assert that the incremental window is not refreshing and that the cached view replayed, which the old refresh would fail.

**Resolved (2db63f7).** In `request_node`'s `Claim::Reused` branch, a claimed node whose `text` was set (`node.text.take().is_some()`) is now `mark_dirty`'d, so Taffy drops the text's cached size when another element takes the key.

`text_replaced_by_another_element_at_its_key_is_laid_out_afresh` reproduces the reviewer's `flex_row` scenario, and the oracle gains `Change::SwapText`. Per the coordinator, the test fails and the layout oracle fails at seed 0 step 11 with the dirtying reverted.

**Resolved (2db63f7).** `TextLeaf` records the text system's `font_generation` (the shared `LineLayoutCache` counter that `add_fonts` bumps) beside `scale_factor`, as `MeasuredUnder`. Any difference forgets the carried measurement and remeasures. `text_is_measured_afresh_after_fonts_are_installed` uses a text system whose lines widen after `add_fonts`.

**Resolved (5b20413).** In `layout` modes:
- `table-stream` pins per frame `leaves_replayed` = 4, `leaves_remeasured` = 4, `leaves_carried` = 312, and zero style writes, children writes and releases.
- The panel scenarios pin `leaves_carried` = (60 − changing) × 65 per frame and `replayed + remeasured` = changing × 65, with zero leaves measured on `still-frame`.

A regression that stopped carry or replay now fails the attribution group.

**Resolved (2db63f7).** The measurement body is now one function, `TextLayout::measure` in `elements/text.rs`. A whitespace-insensitive diff against the old closure shows only the move from captured variables to parameters and `self`; `record_text_measurement_path` is kept. The off path's closure and `fast::text::measure_text` both call it. `set_measure_keeping_clean` and `measure_node` moved out of `taffy.rs` into `fast/layout.rs`.

**Resolved (8b0b0eb).** `draw_roots` wraps its platform reload of `mouse_position`, `modifiers` and `capslock` in `AmbientInput::of` / `stamp_changes`. The reload happens while the window is hovered, dragging or has the pointer captured, and the stamp lands before prepaint, so the frame's replay decisions see it. The activation handler's `modifiers`/`capslock` reload is wrapped the same way.

`dependencies::ambient_input_changed_outside_dispatch_is_stamped` moves the platform pointer, forces the reload through `captured_hitbox`, and requires a recording that read `mouse_position()` to report a change. DEP-1 is amended to name the platform reloads.

**Resolved (8b0b0eb).** `EntityAccessLog.stamping` turns on at the first `begin_recording_dependencies`. Before it does, `note_update`, `note_notify`, `global_changed`, `note_global_inserted`, `note_global_removed` and `AmbientInput::stamp_changes` return after a branch. `note_update` still clears a pending `render_next` mark.

This is sound: a stamp only tells a recording what changed after it began. An update made before stamping started was already seen by any later read, and by the notify rule a later bare notify is not a change.

`an_app_that_never_records_stamps_nothing` asserts that no stamps are held. The spec (DEP-1) records the gate.

**Resolved (8b0b0eb).** `Interactivity::hovered` now documents that it is published, not painted from. It is not a cached-view dependency, and an element that paints by hover must ask `Hitbox::is_hovered`. External `Interactivity` users are told the contract, and FM-6's premise is now stated on the public field.

**Resolved (40b4daf).**
- **The copy.** `Window::reuse_prepaint` gives each copied deferred draw `fast_enclosing = enclosing_retained(self)`, the records open at the copy: the rebuilt views around the reused one.
- **The replay.** `prepaint_deferred_draws` wraps both the built and the replayed branch in `begin_deferred`/`finish_deferred`, so a replayed deferred draw's hitbox range is credited to those records' `deferred_hitboxes`. The ancestors' hover area therefore stays `Own` and they are reused again.
- **Nesting.** `RetainedState.deferred_enclosing`, set by `begin_deferred` and cleared by `finish_deferred`, makes draws deferred or copied from inside a deferred draw belong to the same records.
- **The reused record itself.** It keeps the hover area it was built with, which already covers its deferred hitboxes.

`retained_records::a_copied_deferred_draw_stays_a_part_of_the_views_around_it` encodes the reviewer's `Root > Outer > Inner` popover scenario: 0 views built at first, 2 on the interaction frame, 0 on every still frame after. Per the coordinator, it fails with the copy fix reverted.

**Resolved (285de45).** `splice_prepaint` computes each gap's change in hitboxes: this frame's gap record range minus last frame's. It adds the change to the gap element's DevKit node and to every parent of it whose id lies in a stretch the splice copied (`StretchCopy::copied_devtools_id`), up to the spliced view's root. Nodes outside the spliced view are drawn live and count correctly already.

`splice::devkit_nodes_around_a_gap_count_its_new_hitboxes` reproduces the reviewer's wrapper plus toggled `on_click` scenario. The oracle gains `Change::LeafListener`, which toggles a click listener on the nested leaf without changing its layout key, so the splice oracle now exercises a gap whose hitbox count changes.

**Resolved (285de45).** `ViewElement` now holds `fast::splice::Rebuildable<V>`. The `IntoElement` impls and `cached()` constructors set only a `fn(&V) -> AnyView` pointer. `splice::capture` makes the `AnyView` in `request_layout` only when the window's mode has splice on and view retention is active, so a frame with fast mode off takes no extra entity handle. `note_notified` keeps the notified set only with splice on.

**Resolved.** Lane D ran on an unlocked Mac: `gpux-testkit lane d --grep composition-macos` reports `3 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped` (`artifacts-temp/agentx/gpux-fast-mode/lane-d-composition.log`).
- **Order and bounds:** the native view sits below the overlay at `[40, 50, 160, 100]` at scale 2.
- **Input:** a click passes through when the overlay is empty and beside the open menu, and is taken by the menu.
- **Shadow:** the shadow over the native view reads `[216, 47, 32]` against native `[234, 51, 35]`.

The runtime recorded `check-composition-macos` as passed at revision 89.

**Resolved (ae9c3ab).** `ComposedScene::layer_input_region` returns the overlay layer's primitive bounds clipped by their content masks, without shadows, with overlapping rectangles merged (capped at 32). The AppKit overlay's `hitTest:` takes a point only inside that region, converted from its superview into logical top-left coordinates with the flip honoured. Elsewhere AppKit's hit testing passes through to the native views. A top-layer scrollbar or a tooltip therefore no longer makes a native view unclickable.

`the_overlay_takes_input_only_where_it_draws` covers the region. The lane D input check requires a point beside the open menu, under its shadow, to reach the native view. `docs/fast-mode.md` documents the rule.

Note: the region follows painted content, not hitboxes, so an invisible blocking overlay or a click-outside-to-dismiss surface over a native view no longer intercepts that click. This is the documented trade-off.

**Resolved (ae9c3ab).** Placements are a per-frame `NativeSurfacePlacements` list indexed by `PrepaintStateIndex::fast_native_surfaces_index`. It is copied by `reuse_prepaint` (cached replay and retention) and `StretchCopy::prepaint` (splice), shifted and compared in the retained index helpers, and truncated by `transact`. At present, `show_placed_surfaces` hides surfaces an element placed before when no element places them this frame, and shows them again when one does. It touches only element-placed surfaces, and only on transitions.

`native_surfaces_are_shown_while_their_element_is_drawn` covers off, views and splice modes; per the coordinator it fails with placement reuse disabled. `docs/fast-mode.md` states the visibility rule and that GPUI content masks do not clip native surfaces.

**Resolved (efe96bd).** `crossing_within_window` counts a leave from the overlay window as a move only when the point is inside the overlay's bounds and `lands_on_gpui_content` holds. That means the point is outside every mapped native surface's window bounds, or inside one of the cut-outs applied to that surface, in the surface's own coordinates. Nested natives are checked each against their own bounds.

A pointer moving from an overlay menu straight onto a native child window is now a `MouseExited` for GPUI, as before `57b7401`, while crossings onto GPUI content, including through cut-outs, stay moves.

`fast::composition::x11::tests::a_crossing_onto_a_native_surface_leaves_gpui_content` covers outside, on and through a cut-out, and the case with no natives; it passed in the VM. Lane D passed again at revision 99: X11 with xcompmgr 4/4, Wayland on sway 3/3.

**Resolved (6e7b966).** `docs/upstream/gpui-fast.md` has the section the mapping row at line 74 points to, "Windows base surface spike" (line 81). It names the two options: (a) the wgpu HWND swap chain under a gpux-owned topmost DirectComposition target, and (b) a composition-visual swap chain in the same tree. It says how `composition-windows-resize` measures them and quotes the output of CI run 38050809476 on `79eafd5`.

The recorded result matches the log: both options keep the line at rows 30..33 after the 240 px growth, and both read `[0, 0, 0]` on the newly exposed rows. The section says the resize evidence does not tell the options apart and gives the actual reason for keeping (a): no change to the renderer path, the swap chain or the `DXGI_SCALING_NONE` behaviour of any window, and no second base presentation path.

The lane D log for `6e7b966` (CI run 38052342200) reports the same two measurements, so the document and the check agree.

*Original finding:* the mapping row said "(spike result below)" but no section recorded the spike, its two options or the measured output.

**Resolved (3bff743).** The canvas `pointerleave` handler (`crates/gpui_web/src/events.rs:679`) returns before touching hover state or dispatching `MouseExited` when `fast::composition::stays_in_window` finds the event's `relatedTarget` among this window's own overlay shields. The hook is one full-path call.

Each shield has a `forward_leave` listener (`crates/gpui_web/src/fast/composition.rs:261`). It hands the shield's `pointerleave` to the canvas only when the pointer goes somewhere other than the canvas or a shield. The copy keeps the original `relatedTarget`, so the canvas handler does not suppress it, and a pointer leaving the window from above an overlay still produces one `MouseExited`. A leave with no `relatedTarget` (out of the browser window) is forwarded too.

Proof: the lane B spec "moving between the canvas and the popover stays inside the window" (`tools-node/specs/composition.spec.ts:42`) moves canvas, popover, canvas, clicks the popover and expects `exits 0`. It passes in the revision 110 check log and fails with the hook disabled (`artifacts-temp/ci/laneB-red.log`).

Cursor part: I agree no change is needed. `set_body_cursor` (`crates/gpui_web/src/platform.rs:961`) sets `cursor` on `document.body`. The shield is a child of `body` whose inline styles do not set `cursor`, so it inherits the same value as the window's canvas. On wasm `Window::is_window_hovered` is `is_window_active`, so the platform hover flag does not gate cursor updates there either.

Not a defect, for the record: `is_shield` accepts any element with the shield attribute, not only this window's shields. It differs from the doc comment only for two gpux windows on one page whose shields abut. A browser window's canvas fills the viewport, so that layout does not occur.

*Original finding:* moving the pointer from the canvas onto an overlay's input shield fired the canvas `pointerleave`, which dispatched `MouseExited` and marked the window unhovered while the pointer was still over the window.

findings.descriptionMarkdown:
**Resolved (3bff743).** `crates/gpui_wgpu/src/wgpu_renderer.rs` picks the transparent alpha mode with the plain `pick_alpha_mode(&[PreMultiplied, Inherit])` again. Against the pre-composition base `9ace2ad` the file differs by one line, the `pub(crate)` visibility of the `transparent_alpha_mode` field. A transparent browser window that never composes is configured as it was before the sprint.

The browser override now lives in `crates/gpui_wgpu/src/fast/composition.rs`. `overlay_alpha_mode` is private, and `WgpuRenderer::use_overlay_alpha_mode` is called by the sharing constructors only for a `transparent` surface. When the mode differs it stores it and calls `update_transparency(true)`, which reconfigures the overlay's surface and rebuilds that renderer's own pipelines; the window renderer's pipelines are a separate value and are not touched. Outside the browser `overlay_alpha_mode` returns the picked mode, so native overlays take the same path as before.

Proof: "a popover draws over a DOM element on WebGPU" still passes in the revision 110 lane B log, so the overlay canvas is still premultiplied over the DOM. Lane D on Windows (CI run 38052342200, `6e7b966`) passes with the same constructors.

*Original finding:* `transparent_alpha_mode`, called from the renderer's constructor, forced `PreMultiplied` for every transparent browser WebGPU surface, not only for composition overlays.

findings.descriptionMarkdown:
**Resolved (1a61e91).** `dispatcher()` (`crates/gpui_mobile/src/android/fast/composition.rs:338`) calls `android_jni::platform()` only under `android-native-activity` and otherwise uses the embedded host's platform.

`cargo check -p gpux-mobile --target aarch64-linux-android` passes at `e5b3eb5`; I ran it again myself. It is now the sprint check `check-android-embedded-build`, and the lane E workflow type-checks the default feature set before building the host.

*Original finding:* the default Android build failed with E0425 because the call was not gated.

**Resolved (1a61e91, fa4ac25), by code and documentation; still not run on a device.**

- `Composition.setHostView(View)` names the view GPUI draws into. Containers keep their bounds in GPUI coordinates and `place` adds the host's position in the window.
- Holes and forwarded touches use the container's GPUI bounds, so they no longer depend on the window position.
- The overlay window is sized and placed over the host view, and a layout listener on the host re-places panels and overlay.
- With no host view named, the origin is the window's, which is the NativeActivity case the lane runs.
- `docs/upstream/gpui-fast.md` and `docs/testing.md` now say that only the NativeActivity host has a lane and that no device run covers the embedded host.

*Original finding:* panels were placed in activity-window coordinates with no way to learn the embedded surface's origin.

**Resolved (1a61e91).** `forwardTouches` (`Composition.java:489`) sends a move's historical samples first, each with `getHistoricalEventTime`, then the current sample with `getEventTime`. `native_touch` takes the time and `touch_instant` (`android/fast/composition.rs:269`) converts it from the `uptimeMillis` timeline by its age.

Proof: `composition-android-pan` passes at revision 127 (a swipe on the menu over the native view scrolled it 37 px, with no taps). It runs the cut-out path on GL, which shares `forwardTouches` with the overlay window. The swipe is slow, so the check proves a whole gesture arrives on this path, not the history replay by itself; that part I confirmed by reading.

*Original finding:* forwarded touches dropped batched history and were stamped with the JNI call time.

**Resolved (1a61e91).** `setOrder` (`Composition.java:352`) keeps the panels up to the first position where the mounted and requested orders differ, removes the rest from the top down and mounts the new tail.

Proof: `platform-view-android` adds and disposes a second view and compares the first panel's window through `WindowInspector.getGlobalWindowViews`; it passes at revision 127. You report it red with `kept = 0` forced.

*Original finding:* any change to the order removed and re-added every panel window.

**Resolved (1a61e91).**

- `remove_when_disposed` (`platform_view_element.rs:76`) spawns one foreground task per placed (window, view). `forget` fires its channel, and the task removes the entry and calls `remove_surface` in the window the surface belongs to. It no longer depends on another element's layout, and each window removes its own surface.
- `prepaint` returns early for a disposed handle (line 245), so a view is not re-attached.
- Android asserts the panel window count reaches 0 after dispose; iOS asserts the container left the Metal view. Both pass at revision 127. You report the Android check red with the removal disabled.

*Original finding:* the surface was swept only from a later platform view element's layout, another window's entry was dropped without removal, and no check reached `remove_surface`.

**Resolved (1a61e91).** `platform_view_element` (`platform_view_element.rs:159`) and `ManagedPlatformView::render` (line 354) return `gpui::Div` again. The placing element is private and fills the `Div`, so the caller sizes it as before. The lane scenes size that `Div` and pass.

*Original finding:* `render` returned an unstyleable `AnyElement` with no size, and `platform_view_element` changed its public return type.

**Resolved (1a61e91, fa4ac25).**

- A container whose views take text (a `WebView`, or `onCheckIsTextEditor`) clears `FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE` when touched and watches outside touches (`Composition.java:212`).
- It gives the focus back on a touch outside, the back key, being hidden, leaving the order, or release.
- `nativePanelFocus` sets the flag before the focus moves, and `android/jni.rs:993` does not treat that `LostFocus` as a pause.
- `docs/fast-mode.md` describes the behaviour.

Proof: `platform-view-android-text` passes at revision 127: touching the web view moves the window focus to its panel while the GPUI window stays active, and a touch beside it returns the focus and reaches GPUI.

*Original finding:* panels were never focusable, so native text fields got no soft keyboard, and the docs did not say so.

**Resolved (56a8a4a).**

- `PlatformWindow::rasterizes_layer_tiles` (`crates/gpui/src/platform.rs:1230`) defaults to false, and a window's fast mode is normalized with it at creation and in `set_fast_mode` (`crates/gpui/src/fast/mode.rs`). Only a test window without a renderer answers true (`platform/test/window.rs:368`), so `GPUX_FAST_MODE=1` leaves scroll layers off in every real window until a renderer says otherwise.
- `describe_rendered_frame` describes a frame that composites layers through `expanded_scene` (`crates/gpui/src/fast/layers/paint.rs:997`).
- `lane_a_fast_parity` passes 39 and `lane_c_fast_parity` 77 in the revision 143 check, both now sprint checks. Lane C passes with layers normalized off, which is what PERF-7 states until s11.

*Original finding:* `FastMode::ALL` composited layers no renderer rasterized: 4 lane A and 8 lane C parity tests failed and scroll areas drew blank.

**Resolved (56a8a4a).** `content_view_rendered` (`crates/gpui/src/fast/layers/invalidate.rs:998`) makes a frame in which a view of the content rendered a change, in `scroll_only` and `owner_rerendered_only`.

My two probes from the first review pass at `3027eb3`: the unobserved model (all four variants) and the view reading the pointer both match the reference on every frame, and repaint where they composited before. `layer_carry` gained `a_content_view_whose_render_read_something_that_changed_repaints` (line 775), and the oracle the `Shade` kind with and without a notification.

*Original finding:* a content view rendered again in layout while its container composited, so the frame showed stale content.

**Resolved (56a8a4a).** `owner_change` keeps the owner's own entity in what it read (`invalidate.rs:1102`), and gpux's update tracking counts a lease without a notification as a change while ignoring a bare notify.

My probe passes against both the layers-off reference and fast mode off drawn from scratch. `an_owner_updated_with_the_scroll_repaints` (`layer_carry.rs:331`) and the oracle's `Stripe` kind cover it.

The consequence you asked me to weigh: any lease of the owner between frames, such as a `cx.listener` on its scroll wheel, now repaints. That is correct under the contract (the listener may have changed the view) and the docs say so. It costs composited frames only for views that lease themselves on every scroll.

*Original finding:* the owner was judged only by its notification count, so a silent update with a scroll composited stale content.

**Resolved (56a8a4a).** A `MouseMove` now reaches a layer when the topmost hitbox under the pointer is the content's or the container's own (`crates/gpui/src/fast/layers/input.rs:207`, `holds_hitbox` at line 262). Held moves follow where the press began, and a capture outside the content excludes the layer.

My probe passes: both windows report row 4. Three `layer_carry` tests cover the rule (lines 1677, 1744, 1826). LYR-2 now states it, including that a move does not reach content something else covers.

*Original finding:* a move over content without a hitbox of its own reached listeners holding the bounds they were painted with.

**Resolved (56a8a4a) for a thread that never turns the switch on.** The window-side hooks are gated on the window's switch, the context-free ones on `layers::on_thread()`, and `finish_frame` returns early. My probe on a default window now reads 0 containers and frame counter 0, and `switches::a_window_without_scroll_layers_keeps_none_of_their_books` pins it.

The case of a switch that was on and is off again was `s10-books-kept-after-switch-off`, resolved by `ef9ae14`.

*Original finding:* the hooks were gated on `COMPILED`, so every desktop window did layer bookkeeping with fast mode off.

**Resolved (be30105, amendment at revision 142).** `scroll-same-view` wheels over its hover-styled rows again and asserts no composited frame, every frame counted as repainted or bypassed, and the layer demoted. `scroll-child-view` keeps the gutter. PERF-7 states both cases and refines PERF-2's example to the content's view. The attribution check passes 19 tests at revision 143.

*Original finding:* every div scroll scenario kept the pointer off the rows, and PERF-2's "renders no view" was asserted as one view per frame.

**Resolved (amendment at revision 142).** LYR-1 now says this criterion delivers the desktop targets, that a window also needs a renderer that rasterizes tiles, and which criteria add the renderers, the browser and mobile.

*Original finding:* LYR-1 said every gpux renderer while the code compiled layers for desktop only.

**Resolved (ef9ae14).** `ON_THREAD` is now a count of the thread's windows with scroll layers on (`crates/gpui/src/fast/layers/mod.rs:47`). `mode::counted` (`crates/gpui/src/fast/mode.rs:263`) moves it on every transition, at window creation and in `set_fast_mode`, the only two places a window's mode is written, and `Drop for WindowFastMode` (line 272) takes a closing window out.
